title: VPC: subnets, CIDR ranges, public and private

videos.script: Every network in this course lives inside a VPC. {{vpc}} A VPC is a range of private addresses. It belongs to one account, in one region. Your account already has one in every region, made for you. {{default}} This lesson explains why the shop leaves that one alone. Then it builds the shop's own: ten dot twenty, slash sixteen, across the three zones of São Paulo. {{plan}} The range is cut into smaller ranges called subnets. There is one per zone, and one per job. A short Python program does the cutting, so nobody does binary arithmetic by hand. {{reserved}} Every subnet then gives five of its addresses to AWS. You will check that number against moto. {{refused}} Some subnets are refused, and the refusals teach the rules. {{public}} And one word is used wrongly almost everywhere. That word is public. A subnet is not public because of its name, or because of a setting on it. It is public because of where its route table sends traffic. Right now, all nine of the shop's subnets are private. The next lesson changes that, on purpose, for three of them. {{end}}
